summary: In Martha’s home, Jesus defends Mary for sitting at His feet while Martha frets over serving: Mary has chosen the one thing needed.
key_insight: Martha asked Jesus to send Mary back to help. He refused, and said Mary’s place at His feet “will not be taken away from her.” Martha’s trouble was not her serving but being “worried and troubled about many things.”
story: As Jesus and His disciples traveled, He came to a village where a woman named Martha welcomed Him into her house. She had a sister called Mary, who sat at Jesus’ feet and listened to His word.
But Martha was distracted with much serving. She came to Jesus and said, “Lord, do You not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Therefore tell her to help me.”
Jesus answered her, “Martha, Martha, you are worried and troubled about many things. But one thing is needed, and Mary has chosen that good part, which will not be taken away from her.”

scene.label: The village
scene.text: Luke does not name it. John tells us that Martha and Mary lived in Bethany, on the Mount of Olives just outside Jerusalem, with their brother Lazarus (John 11:1, 18).

scene.label: A host’s work
scene.text: Luke calls it Martha’s house, and she was the host. If His disciples came in with Him, as they usually did, welcoming them meant a full meal for a dozen or more guests, all made by hand.

scene.label: At His feet
scene.text: Sitting at a teacher’s feet was the place of a disciple; Paul was brought up “at the feet of Gamaliel” (Acts 22:3). Mary took the disciple’s place, and Jesus defended her right to it.

scene.label: Serving
scene.text: Luke’s word for Martha’s serving is the word from which deacon comes, and Luke honors that work elsewhere (Luke 8:3; 22:27). The problem Jesus names is not the work but the distraction.

witnesses.luke: Only Luke tells this story, and he places it right after the Good Samaritan. The lawyer had quoted two commands: love God and love your neighbor. The Samaritan shows the second in action; Mary, listening at Jesus’ feet, shows where the first begins.

seeing.reveals: Jesus welcomes a woman to sit and learn at His feet as His disciple, and He loves the busy host enough to tell her the truth about her heart.
seeing.living: Work done for Jesus can crowd out time with Jesus. Martha’s question, “do You not care,” came from a distracted heart, not a lazy one. Begin where Mary sat, and let your serving flow from listening rather than from worry.
seeing.ponder: What “many things” are pulling you away from the one thing Jesus says is needed?

preaching.big_idea: Busy service can crowd out Jesus; the one thing needed is to sit at His feet.
preaching.watch_for: Jesus says Martha’s name twice, as He later says “Simon, Simon” (Luke 22:31) and the risen Lord says “Saul, Saul” (Acts 9:4). The doubled name is tender and urgent, not harsh.
